summary: Streaming chat connection goes silent mid-response during live model swap on Dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Customer reports SSE chat sessions receiving an initial stream of tokens and then entering a prolonged silent period (~30-90s) without socket close or error. Client eventually times out. Impact: High — production traffic for Nimbus Finance experienced multiple user-facing interruptions for multi-turn assistant sessions during peak business hours. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for Nimbus Finance in us-west-2 running quantized llama-2-13b model variant. Observed at ~2026-03-12 15:04 PDT during a staged live model swap triggered by platform rollout automation.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer sent streaming POST /v1/chat/completions to the dedicated endpoint with max_tokens=2048 and stream=true.
2) Request produced several SSE chunks, then no bytes for ~45s while the TCP connection remained ESTABLISHED.
3) Client retried and sometimes received resumed tokens if routed to original worker, but most retries hit the silent period.
4) Issue reproduced only when rollout overlapped with high concurrency (sustained QPS in dedicated pool), not on single-client tests.
logs:
serving-runtime logs (excerpt):
[2026-03-12T22:04:12Z] INFO routing: request assigned to worker w-17
[2026-03-12T22:04:12Z] INFO runtime: start stream for request r-9dfa
[2026-03-12T22:04:15Z] INFO runtime: streamed chunk 1 for r-9dfa
[2026-03-12T22:04:16Z] INFO scheduler: initiating model-swap canary rollout job job-449
[2026-03-12T22:04:18Z] WARN routing: rebalancer moving in-flight requests away from w-17 to w-24
[2026-03-12T22:04:18Z] INFO proxy: handoff request r-9dfa from w-17 -> w-24
[2026-03-12T22:04:18Z] INFO w-24: loading model llm-v2-13b-q4 (disk I/O spike)
[2026-03-12T22:04:18Z] ERROR w-24: stall detected: no streamed output for r-9dfa for 34s
[2026-03-12T22:04:52Z] INFO routing: request r-9dfa re-routed back to w-17 (original)
[2026-03-12T22:04:53Z] INFO runtime: resumed stream for r-9dfa
Stack traces show blocking disk reads and long-lived synchronous lock in model loader during the handoff sequence.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis focused on proxy buffering or client-side keepalive. Reproduced internally when we simulated a live model swap while concurrent streams were in-flight on the dedicated pool. Observed correlation between the 'model-swap canary' orchestration action and stalls. Handoff path involves proxy-level in-memory transfer of routing metadata; however, the target worker w-24 performed synchronous file-based model loading which saturated local IO and blocked the streaming handshake. The serving-runtime does not currently drain or hold streaming sockets during worker replacement; handoff results in the request being routed to a worker that cannot immediately produce tokens. Also noted scheduler started a model preload but allowed routing to assign requests before preload completed.
mitigation_actions:
1) Rolled back the canary model-swap deployment at 2026-03-12T22:06Z which restored stable behavior for in-flight sessions.
2) Applied a temporary routing policy: disable handoff for streams flagged as 'long-lived' until worker preload completes (hotfix pushed to routing layer).
3) Opened INT ticket for scheduler change to mark nodes 'not ready for streaming' until model preload finished.
next_steps:
- Engineering to add a streaming-safe handoff protocol: either pause routing of in-flight streaming sessions or ensure target worker preloads model into memory before accepting handoffs.
- Improve observability: emit 'handoff_latency' metric and alert when handoff stalls exceed 5s.
- Scheduler: change to 'preload-only' node state that blocks routing for streaming until model load complete.
- Postmortem and customer follow-up to describe root cause and timeline.

resolution: Mitigated by rolling back the live model swap and applying a temporary routing safeguard. Permanent fixes planned: streaming-safe handoff protocol, scheduler preload gating, and additional metrics/alerts. Customer notified and monitoring in place.
